text:
Eli: Heads-up — noticed rack eu-west1-rack8 had staggered GPU resets starting ~00:03 UTC, causing p99 inference spikes on a few customer routes. Anyone watching?

Maria: saw the alerts. DCGM showing intermittent Xid 13 and powercap toggles on cards 0/2/4. temps look fine-ish (72-78C) but 12V rail current is oscillating.

OpsBot: [ALERT] node-ew1-rack8-03: GPU reset detected (count=4) — automated drain recommended.

Hana: can you paste the BMC/PSU logs? might be PSU hysteresis with multiple cards hitting a threshold and PSUs cycling powercap.

Eli: logs: 
```
BMC: PSU1_voltage_drop 11.8V -> 11.2V
PSU: AC_LOAD_SPIKE 47A at 00:02:41
nvidia: Xid(13) on GPU0 kernel: GPC stall
nvidia-smi: power limit changed from 300W -> 220W
```

Sam: interesting — fan PWM stable, so not classic thermal runaway. More like rail sag under transient concurrent token bursts. We had a batch of 512 long-seq requests around 00:02 causing temporary surge.

David: is this widespread? capacity-wise we need to decide: drain nodes or live-migrate inference to dedicated pool. eu-west1 spare GPUs are limited today.

Maria: scope: 3 nodes in rack8 with 2-3 affected cards each. Other racks in eu-west1 show no railing. Could be a PSU bank failing under brief load bursts.

Hana: quick mitigation: reduce max concurrent seq length on affected routes to cap surge and cordon the three nodes. I'll patch the routing policy now to route new requests to us-west1/dedicated fallback.

Eli: thanks. Also tagging infra-oncall for physical triage tomorrow. If PSU is flaky we'll swap PSUs, but need drain plan to avoid KV cache thrash.

OpsBot: deploy started: routing patch -> 2m. Canary ok.

Sam: follow-up telemetry: after routing patch, resets stopped but p99 still slightly elevated due to warmup of KV caches on fallback nodes. Expected to normalize in ~15-30m. Notifying support for potential customer impact.

Maria: action items: 1) cordon node-ew1-rack8-{02,03,07} 2) open hardware ticket HWS-2897 for PSU bank on rack8 3) gather full BMC traces and correlate with request bursts 4) consider firmware bump on PSUs if vendor has micro-hysteresis fix.

David: cost note — routing to dedicated will burn through committed capacity quickly. Marking these routes as 'degraded' in console to surface to customers and avoid surprise billing.

Hana: for triage tomorrow I'll bring a logger to capture high-res current samples and run synthetic long-seq load to reproduce. If we can reproduce, we can tune batching/queueing at router to avoid simultaneous surges.

Eli: temporary remediation timeline: cordon + routing patch done (00:05), monitor for 2h. Hardware swap scheduled in next available on-site maintenance window (48h) unless remote firmware/KMS update fixes it.

Maria: leaving notes in the runbook and adding eval prompts to detect similar patterns (simultaneous high-token bursts + small fan while PSU current spikes).

Sam: thanks — will follow up with a short postmortem draft if the hardware swap happens.

Eli: ping @David @Hana @Maria when you've added logs to HWS-2897.

David: noted.

OpsBot: Incident HWS-2897 created. Severity: P2.

Eli: end.
